blocks.text: Cut-off criteria

Processes whose total contribution is less than 1% of the total mass and primary energy of the declared or functional unit may be excluded, provided that the total of excluded flows does not exceed 5% of mass and energy per module. No known flows were deliberately excluded.
Allocation

Where a manufacturing site produces several products, energy, materials and wastes were allocated on a mass basis. Recycled content enters the system burden-free (cut-off approach); burdens of material recycling at end of life are attributed to the system that uses the secondary material.
Data sources and data quality

Primary data was collected from the manufacturer for the reference year. Background data was taken from the LCI database listed in the declaration summary, selected for technological, geographical and temporal representativeness.
The LCA was modelled in EcoMetric 1.0 using ecoinvent 3.12 cut-off.
All results are given per 1 m² of stone wool insulation with a thermal resistance of RSI = 1 m²·K/W.
X = module declared; MND = module not declared; ND = not declared. Results for modules A1–A3, A4, A5, B, C and D should not be summed.

blocks.text: Biogenic carbon
Biogenic carbon is reported separately as GWP-biogenic in accordance with EN 15804+A2. Biogenic carbon content of the product and its packaging is declared where it exceeds 5% of the product mass.
Contribution analysis
The interpretation is based on EN 15804+A2 (EF 3.1) results.

The product stage (A1–A3) accounts for 92.0% of global warming potential — total across the declared modules, excluding module D. Module A1–A3 — Product stage contributes 92.0% of total global warming potential — total. Module A1–A3 — Product stage contributes 92.0% of total global warming potential — fossil fuels. Module A5 — Assembly / installation contributes 50.0% of total global warming potential — biogenic. Module A1–A3 — Product stage contributes 92.4% of total global warming potential — land use and land use change. Module A1–A3 — Product stage contributes 92.1% of total depletion potential of the stratospheric ozone layer. Module A1–A3 — Product stage contributes 92.8% of total acidification potential, accumulated exceedance. Module A1–A3 — Product stage contributes 92.2% of total eutrophication potential — freshwater. Module A1–A3 — Product stage contributes 91.6% of total eutrophication potential — marine. Module A1–A3 — Product stage contributes 92.0% of total eutrophication potential — terrestrial. Module A1–A3 — Product stage contributes 91.4% of total formation potential of tropospheric ozone. Module A1–A3 — Product stage contributes 91.4% of total abiotic depletion potential — minerals and metals. Module A1–A3 — Product stage contributes 91.6% of total abiotic depletion potential — fossil resources. Module A1–A3 — Product stage contributes 92.2% of total water (user) deprivation potential.

blocks.text: Assumptions

The selection of secondary datasets to represent the supply chain is a significant value choice; no generic dataset is a perfect fit. Supply-chain-specific data would improve the accuracy of the results.
Limitations
Results represent potential environmental impacts and do not predict impacts on specific endpoints, the exceedance of thresholds, safety margins or risks.

EPDs of construction products may not be comparable if they do not comply with EN 15804 and if they are not compared in a building context. Environmental declarations from different programs (ISO 14025) may not be comparable. Comparison of the environmental performance of products using EPD information shall be based on the product's use and impacts at the building level.
